overall_status: useful restricted algebraic construction; not a mission-level discovery

claims.claim: If L:R->F_2^k is surjective, vectors d_j in the common radical with L(d_j)=e_j certify an exact one-shot uniform sampler for every simultaneous target fiber; every fiber has size 2^(n-k).
claims.scope: Supplied explicit Boolean quadratic forms over F_2 and a supplied target.
limitations: Surjectivity of L is sufficient but not necessary for equal fibers.
The theorem does not solve model acquisition or ordinal/comparison learning.

claims.claim: The vector map F has equal nonempty fibers iff every nonzero linear combination of its coordinate quadratics is balanced; for quadratic forms, balance is equivalent to a nonzero normalized restriction on the polar radical.
claims.scope: Exact characterization; checking all output combinations may take exponential time in k.
limitations: The characterization alone gives only expected 2^k rejection sampling for a target.
Do not infer a polynomial-time sampler for arbitrary vectorial quadratic maps.

claims.claim: Individual balance does not imply simultaneous target availability or equal joint-fiber sizes; deficient common-radical rank also does not imply failure of equal fibers.
limitations: Examples are mathematical counterexamples, not empirical evidence.

claims.claim: Exhaustive n=3 enumeration validates the balance criterion and common-radical sampler statement for all ordered pairs of balanced quadratic Boolean functions on three bits.
limitations: Finite checks do not replace the proof or establish novelty.

claims.claim: This common-radical right-inverse sampler is novel.
limitations: The construction is an elementary group action and extends an inherited single-fiber toggle.
Bounded search found adjacent prior art but did not establish priority.

acquisition_and_cost.preprocessing: O(k*n^3) classical binary bit operations, with forms given explicitly
acquisition_and_cost.one_shot_sampling: n fair random bits plus O(k*n^2) direct quadratic evaluation and O(k*n) correction operations
